articles.title: What is Google’s AI-built zero-day story? #tech
articles.summary: Google confirms hackers wielded AI to craft a zero-day that bypassed 2FA — because apparently our robot overlords decided to start with cybercrime instead of world domination. The age of AI-assisted exploitation has officially begun, and it's terrifyingly efficient.

articles.title: Help EFF Solve an Issue That's Bigger than Creepy Ads
articles.summary: Microsoft's April Patch Tuesday delivered a staggering 167 vulnerabilities including a SharePoint zero-day and the deliciously named 'BlueHammer' Windows Defender flaw. Meanwhile, Chrome patched its fourth zero-day of the year because apparently browsers are made of Swiss cheese.

articles.title: Anti-DDoS Firm Heaped Attacks on Brazilian ISPs
articles.summary: Canvas got pwned hard by ransomware goons who defaced login pages nationwide, disrupting education for millions. Nothing says 'modern learning' like having your homework held hostage by cybercriminals with questionable grammar skills.

articles.title: California colleges went big on online learning tools. Then the worst happened
articles.summary: Instructure rolled over and paid ShinyHunters after the Canvas breach hit 9,000+ schools. Because apparently negotiating with ransomware gangs is now considered 'responsible incident response' in corporate America.

articles.title: Victory! End-to-End Encrypted RCS Comes to Apple and Android Chats
articles.summary: Instagram officially murdered its end-to-end encryption feature, proving once again that Facebook's privacy promises have the shelf life of a mayonnaise sandwich in the desert. Meta's commitment to user privacy remains as mythical as a unicorn.

articles.title: EFF Launches New Offline Campaign for Saudi Wikipedian Osama Khalid
articles.summary: Victory lap time: Apple finally enabled E2E encryption for RCS, meaning iPhone-Android chats can now be properly private. Only took them roughly a decade to stop being petty about cross-platform security.

articles.title: Checkbox Assessments Aren't Fit to Measure to Risk
articles.summary: EFF launches campaign for Saudi Wikipedian Osama Khalid, who started editing Wikipedia at age 12 and became a freedom-of-information warrior. Because apparently contributing to human knowledge is now a crime in authoritarian hellscapes.

articles.title: Malware crew TeamPCP open-sources its Shai-Hulud worm on GitHub
articles.summary: Mystery leaker 'YellowKey' keeps dropping Microsoft zero-days like confetti, with their latest potentially turning stolen laptops into goldmines of corporate secrets. Someone's having way too much fun embarrassing Redmond's security team.

articles.title: Mystery Microsoft bug leaker keeps the zero-days coming
articles.summary: Bug hunter discovers three massive MCP database flaws affecting Apache and Alibaba systems, but one vendor apparently thinks ignoring security researchers is a viable business strategy. Spoiler alert: it's not.

articles.title: Patch Tuesday, April 2026 Edition
articles.summary: Scattered Spider's 'Tylerb' pleads guilty to wire fraud and identity theft after their 2022 SMS phishing spree that made cybersecurity professionals weep into their coffee. Another script kiddie learns that 'it's just a prank bro' isn't a legal defense.
